- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is trending down.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days), especially if sentiment was neutral or negative prior — cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model often fails to correct — reduce forecast slope in subsequent days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out forecast if sentiment swings sharply within 5 days.
- If sentiment history includes multiple negative entries followed by a positive spike, model often undercorrects — anticipate a rebound and adjust forecast upward by 2–5%.
- When sentiment is mixed (±0.5), model often averages out — avoid overfitting to recent sentiment; use weighted average of 3–5 prior days instead.
